purpose: Fetch NASCAR-related data (drivers, photos, stats, news, scoreboards, schedules, results, standings) from the NASCAR Motorsport API on RapidAPI.

notes: Use api_key = os.getenv("RAPIDAPI_KEY") in code. Do NOT hardcode the key.
Some HTTP frameworks add extra headers automatically. If requests fail unexpectedly, remove non-essential headers and retry.

caching.provider_note: API uses caching for race results to enhance performance and reduce server load.
client_guidance: Do not assume data is live to-the-second for historical endpoints.
If your app needs a refresh button, allow users to re-fetch and overwrite cached client state.

endpoints.name: driver_photos
endpoints.description: Retrieves photos of a specific driver with support for pagination.

endpoints.name: driver_stats
endpoints.description: Retrieves detailed statistics for a specified driver (by year).

endpoints.name: athlete_info
endpoints.description: Retrieves detailed information about a specific athlete.

endpoints.name: news
endpoints.description: Retrieves NASCAR news articles with pagination.

endpoints.name: current_scoreboard
endpoints.description: Retrieves the most recent scoreboard data (multi-league motor sports feed structure).

endpoints.name: scoreboard
endpoints.description: Retrieves scoreboard data for a specified year, with optional month/day filters.

endpoints.name: race_report
endpoints.description: Retrieves the race report for a specific race.

endpoints.name: race_results_by_driver_year
endpoints.description: Retrieves race results for a specific driver and year.

endpoints.name: results_by_year_series
endpoints.description: Retrieves race results for the specified year and series.

endpoints.name: standings_drivers
endpoints.description: Retrieves driver standings for a specific year.

endpoints.name: schedule
endpoints.description: Retrieves schedule data for the specified year.

status_code_map.agent_action: Validate required query params are present and correctly formatted.
Confirm RAPIDAPI_KEY env var is set and headers include x-rapidapi-key and x-rapidapi-host.
Check plan limits/permissions; if rate-limited, backoff and retry.
Verify endpoint path and parameter values (IDs/year/series).
Backoff and retry; add client-side rate limiting.
Retry after short delay; if persistent, surface error details.
Retry with backoff; treat as transient outage.

implementation_notes: Build a thin client wrapper: request(endpoint_name, params) -> JSON.
Validate required params before calling the API.
Normalize types: keep driverId/athleteId/raceId/year as strings unless the endpoint specifies number.
For fantasy league use cases, likely core endpoints are: /results (by year/series), /standings-drivers (by year), /schedule (by year), /stats (driverId), /athlete-info (athleteId), /news.
